Good news- Open Enrollment Is Passive This Year!

If you are happy with your current benefits, you don't need to do anything. Your existing benefit elections will automatically carry over into the new plan year. This is called a passive enrollment. However, we encourage you to explore the new benefits and coverage options available this year. If you want to add, remove, or change any benefits, you must make those changes during the Open Enrollment period.

Please Note: Flexible Spending Accounts (FSA) Require Annual Re-Enrollment. If you wish to participate in a Health Care FSA or Dependent Care FSA for the upcoming plan year, you must actively make a new election during Open Enrollment. Current FSA elections will not automatically roll over.

Flexible Spending Accounts

Spending Accounts

Use pre-tax dollars to pay for health care, dependent care and commuting, and keep more of your paycheck.

Spending accounts

Pre-tax dollars, smarter spending.

FSA

Make every dollar go further. Set aside pre-tax money for medical, dental, vision and dependent care costs, and save roughly 25 cents on every dollar you spend.

Flexible Spending Accounts

Contribute what you expect to spend during the plan year; unused funds are generally forfeited.

Healthcare FSA

A Flexible Spending Account (FSA) lets you set aside money from your paycheck, before taxes, to pay for eligible health care expenses. You can use it to buy everyday items like pain relievers, allergy medicine, cold medicine, bandages, sunscreen, and other eligible over-the-counter (OTC) products. You do NOT have to enroll in your employer's medical insurance to participate in an FSA! You can have an FSA even if you have medical coverage somewhere else or no medical coverage at all. Remember, USE IT OR LOSE IT! Any money left in your account after the plan's deadline may be forfeited, so plan carefully when deciding how much to contribute.

Browse the full eligibility list at the FSA Store.

Dependent Care FSA

Use your Dependent Care FSA funds to pay for eligible care expenses for children under age 13 or qualifying adult dependents who are unable to care for themselves. Eligible expenses may include daycare, before- and after-school care, summer day camps (overnight camps are not eligible), and adult daycare that allow you (and your spouse, if applicable) to work or look for work.

Commuter Benefits – Parking & Transit

Save money on your daily commute by using pre-tax dollars to pay for eligible parking and public transportation expenses. For 2027, you can set aside a projected $350 per month for parking and an additional $350 per month for transit, including buses, trains, and eligible vanpools. That's up to $700 per month in pre-tax savings opportunities, helping you reduce your taxable income and keep more of your paycheck!

A Paycheck Tale: Bob vs. Tom

Bob and Tom work side-by-side at the same company, each earning an annual salary of $52,000 ($2,000 gross per paycheck). Both men expect to spend about $1,300 a year ($50 per pay period) on predictable medical expenses like prescriptions, dental checkups, and new glasses.

During open enrollment, Bob enrolled in a Health FSA, while Tom decided not to enroll, thinking it was safer to just pay out of pocket.

Here is exactly how that single choice plays out over their 26 pay periods:

Pay Period vs. Annual FSA Comparison (26 Pay Periods)

FeaturePer Pay PeriodAnnual Total
Tom (No FSA)Bob (With FSA)Tom (No FSA)Bob (With FSA)
Gross Pay$2,000.00$2,000.00$52,000.00$52,000.00
Pre-tax FSA Deduction$0.00-$50.00$0.00-$1,300.00
Taxable Income$2,000.00$1,950.00$52,000.00$50,700.00
Estimated Taxes (30%)-$600.00-$585.00-$15,600.00-$15,210.00
Out-of-Pocket Medical Cost-$50.00$0.00-$1,300.00$0.00
Net Take-Home Pay$1,350.00$1,365.00$35,100.00$35,490.00
Total Annual Value Kept$35,100.00$35,490.00
Total Annual SavingsTom's Baseline+$390.00

How the Math Turns in Bob's Favor

  • The Tax Shield: Because Bob uses an FSA, the government only taxes him on $1,950 each pay period. Tom gets taxed on the full $2,000. Over the year, the IRS takes $15,600.00 from Tom, but only $15,210.00 from Bob.
  • The Bottom Line: Bob shields $1,300.00 of his hard-earned income from taxes. By doing this, he pays for his medical costs entirely tax-free, outperforming Tom's strategy and keeping an extra $390.00 cash in his pocket by the end of the year.

Action required over $150,000

Evidence of Insurability (EOI) form

If you elect more than $150,000 in coverage when you first enroll, or wish to increase your current coverage amount more than $10,000, you must complete an Evidence of Insurability (EOI) form. Coverage up to $150,000 is guaranteed when you enroll on time; the amount above it starts once MetLife approves your form.

  1. Download the form and print it.
  2. Fill it out completely and sign it by hand.
  3. Scan it and email it to SOHSubmissions@metlife.com with the subject line Key HR 233450-EOI Form.
Open the form in a new tab

You can also fax it to 859.225.7909 or mail it to MetLife Statement of Health Unit, P.O. Box 14069, Lexington, KY 40512-4069. Questions? Call MetLife at 800.638.6420, prompt 1, or email eoi@metlifeservice.com.

Supplemental coverage

Hospital Indemnity Insurance

Hospital indemnity insurance pays a fixed cash benefit directly to you when you have a qualifying hospital stay.

Unlike a medical plan, which pays doctors and hospitals based on negotiated rates and itemized bills, hospital indemnity pays you a set dollar amount for specific hospital events, no matter what your medical plan covers.

How it works

Simple, flexible cash when it is needed most

  • Cash paid directly to youBenefits go straight to you by check or direct deposit. Use the money for deductibles, copays and coinsurance, or everyday costs like rent, groceries, childcare and lost wages during recovery.
  • No network restrictionsHospital indemnity is not tied to a provider network, so your benefit is the same at any hospital, in or out of network.
  • Pays on top of other coverageBenefits are paid in addition to any medical plan, workers' compensation and other supplemental plans like accident or critical illness, with no reduction.
  • Simple claimsNo complex medical coding. Submit a claim form with your hospital admission and discharge paperwork and get paid quickly.

Why it matters

Why hospital indemnity is worth considering

Help with out-of-pocket costs

A hospital stay can leave you facing thousands in out-of-pocket costs. Hospital indemnity helps bridge that gap for a modest payroll deduction.

Valued by growing families

Many group plans waive waiting periods for pregnancy, so if you enroll during open enrollment you can receive a cash benefit when your baby arrives. It is one of the most appreciated voluntary benefits for growing families.

Guaranteed issue and portable

When you enroll at hire or during open enrollment, coverage is typically guaranteed issue, with no medical exams or health questions. Most plans are portable, so you can keep your coverage if you leave.

One day in the hospital averages $3,132. Hospital indemnity helps you cover the costs your medical plan does not, so a hospital stay never has to become a financial setback. Source: KFF analysis of AHA data, 2023

Benefits glossary

Glossary

A clear, practical guide to the plan types, costs and accounts you will see during open enrollment.

Plan Types & Network Models

HMO Health Maintenance Organization

A managed care plan where all non-emergency care must come from a defined local network of providers.

Network & referrals
You choose an in-network Primary Care Physician (PCP), and you need a PCP referral to see a specialist.
Out-of-network
Not covered, except for life-threatening emergencies.
Cost
Lowest premiums and lower copays, with the least provider flexibility.

PPO Preferred Provider Organization

A flexible plan with a broad network of preferred doctors and facilities, plus partial coverage for out-of-network care.

Network & referrals
No PCP required. You can see specialists directly without a referral.
Out-of-network
Covered, but with separate, higher deductibles and coinsurance.
Cost
Highest premiums in exchange for the most freedom to choose providers.

EPO Exclusive Provider Organization

Combines the direct specialist access of a PPO with the network limits of an HMO.

Network & referrals
No PCP or specialist referrals needed, but care is covered only at in-network providers.
Out-of-network
Not covered, except emergencies. You pay 100% for non-emergency out-of-network care.
Cost
Moderate premiums, lower than PPOs and similar to HMOs.

POS Point of Service

Combines HMO-style coordinated care with the option to go out of network like a PPO.

Network & referrals
You choose an in-network PCP and get PCP referrals for specialist visits.
Out-of-network
Covered. If your PCP refers you, the plan pays more. If you go on your own, coverage drops and you may need to file the claim yourself.
Cost
Moderate premiums with PCP-coordinated care.

Costs & How You Pay

Premium

The fixed amount paid each month to keep your coverage active, whether or not you use care. With employer plans, the cost is usually split between the employer and your pre-tax payroll deduction.

Deductible

The amount you pay each plan year for covered services before the plan starts paying.

Embedded
On a family plan, each person has their own deductible. Once one person meets it, the plan starts paying for them even if the family total is not met.
Aggregate
The full family deductible must be met before the plan pays coinsurance for anyone on the plan.

Copayment (Copay)

A flat dollar amount you pay at the time of service, for example $25 for primary care or $15 for a generic prescription. Copays are predictable, usually are not subject to the deductible and count toward your out-of-pocket maximum.

Coinsurance

Your percentage share of covered costs after you meet the deductible. On an 80/20 plan, the plan pays 80% of the allowed amount and you pay 20% until you reach your out-of-pocket maximum.

Out-of-Pocket Maximum

The most you will pay for covered in-network care in a plan year. Deductibles, copays and coinsurance all count toward it. Premiums, out-of-network balance bills and non-covered services do not. Once you reach it, the plan pays 100% of allowed in-network costs for the rest of the year.

Allowed Amount & Balance Billing

Allowed amount
The maximum payment the insurer and an in-network provider have agreed on for a service.
Balance billing
When an out-of-network provider bills you for the difference between their full charge and the allowed amount. The federal No Surprises Act prohibits this for emergency care and other care you could not choose.

Tax-Advantaged Healthcare Accounts

FSA Health Care Flexible Spending Account

Who owns it
Employer-owned. Stays with the company if you leave.
Who can contribute
Employee and/or employer
Plan requirement
Available with any plan, or no plan
Rollover rules
Use it or lose it, subject to a grace period or limited carryover.

Dependent Care FSA

Who owns it
Employer-owned. Stays with the company.
Who can contribute
Employee and/or employer
Plan requirement
Available with any health plan
Rollover rules
Use it or lose it. Covers qualifying child and elder day care.

HRA Health Reimbursement Arrangement

Who owns it
Employer-owned and 100% employer-funded.
Who can contribute
Employer only
Plan requirement
Set by the employer
Rollover rules
Set by the employer's plan document.

Enrollment Rules & Protections

Qualifying Life Event (QLE)

A major life change that lets you change your benefits outside of open enrollment, also called a Special Enrollment Period.

Common events
Marriage, divorce, birth or adoption, death of a covered dependent, or losing other group coverage, such as when a spouse changes jobs.
Timeline
Changes generally must be made within 30 days of the event, or 60 days for loss of Medicaid or CHIP.

Section 125 / Cafeteria Plan

The IRS rule that lets your premiums and FSA contributions come out of your paycheck before federal income, Social Security and Medicare taxes. Because of this rule, once open enrollment closes your elections are locked in for the full plan year unless you have a qualifying life event.

Prior Authorization & Step Therapy

Prior authorization
Your provider must get the insurer's approval, showing medical necessity, before a procedure, surgery or specialty drug is covered.
Step therapy
You may need to try a lower-cost or generic drug first before the plan covers a higher-cost brand.

Formulary & Drug Tiers

The formulary is your plan's list of covered prescription drugs.

Tier 1
Generic. Lowest cost, with the same active ingredients as the brand name.
Tier 2
Preferred brand. Brand-name drugs on the plan's preferred list.
Tier 3
Non-preferred brand. Higher-cost brands when a generic or preferred option exists.
Tier 4
Specialty. High-cost biologics, injectables and complex therapies, often requiring prior authorization.

Summary of Benefits and Coverage (SBC)

A standard document required by the Affordable Care Act for every plan. It lists covered services, deductibles and copays, with sample cost scenarios such as having a baby, so you can compare plans side by side.

Voluntary & Supplemental Benefits

Short-Term Disability (STD)

Replaces part of your weekly income, typically 50% to 70%, after a short waiting period if a non-work illness, injury or recovery from childbirth keeps you from working.

Long-Term Disability (LTD)

Replaces part of your monthly income when a disability lasts beyond the short-term period, typically starting after 90 or 180 days, until you recover, reach retirement age or hit the benefit limit.

Critical Illness Insurance

Pays a lump-sum cash benefit directly to you when you are diagnosed with a covered illness such as cancer, heart attack or stroke, separate from your health plan.

Accident Insurance

Pays set cash amounts for accidental injuries and related care, such as ER visits, fractures, dislocations and concussions.

Hospital Indemnity

Pays a fixed cash benefit directly to you for each day you are admitted to the hospital, helping cover high deductibles.

EAP (Employee Assistance Program)

A free, confidential program offering short-term counseling, legal consultations and financial wellness support for you and your household.

Required Notices

Federal law requires us to share the following notices with you. Please read them and keep a copy for your records.

Questions? 800.922.4133 | Benefits@KeyHRO.com

1

Health Insurance Marketplace Notice

What is the Health Insurance Marketplace?

The Marketplace is designed to help you find health insurance that meets your needs and fits your budget. The Marketplace offers "one-stop shopping" to find and compare private health insurance options. You may also be eligible for a tax credit that lowers your monthly premium right away. Open enrollment for health insurance coverage through the Marketplace begins November 1 for coverage starting as early as January 1.

Can I save money on my health insurance premiums in the Marketplace?

You may qualify to save money and lower your monthly premium, but only if your employer does not offer health coverage, or offers coverage that doesn't meet certain standards. The savings on your premium that you're eligible for depends on your household income.

Does employer health coverage affect eligibility for premium savings through the Marketplace?

Yes. If you have an offer of health coverage from your employer that meets certain standards, you will not be eligible for a tax credit through the Marketplace. However, you may be eligible for a tax credit that lowers your monthly premium, or a reduction in certain cost-sharing, if your employer does not offer coverage to you at all or does not offer coverage that meets certain standards. If the cost of a plan from your employer that would cover you (and not any other members of your family) is more than 10.22% of your household income for the year (this percentage may change annually), or if the coverage your employer provides does not meet the "minimum value" standard set by the Affordable Care Act, you may be eligible for a tax credit. An employer-sponsored health plan meets the "minimum value" standard if the plan's share of the total allowed benefit costs covered by the plan is no less than 60% of such costs.

Note: If you purchase a health plan through the Marketplace instead of accepting health coverage offered by your employer, then you may lose the employer contribution (if any) to the employer-offered coverage. Also, your employee contribution to employer-offered coverage is often pre-tax. Marketplace premiums are paid after-tax.

How can I get more information?

Please visit HealthCare.gov for more information about Marketplace coverage and its cost, your eligibility for tax credits, and an online application. You may also request more information from either Key HR or your worksite employer. If you are eligible for health insurance coverage through your worksite employer, you will receive enrollment and eligibility information separately and possibly at a different time of year. If you are eligible for health insurance coverage through Key HR, enrollment and eligibility information is enclosed. If it is not enclosed with this communication, contact your worksite employer for details.

¿Qué es el Mercado de Seguros Médicos?

El Mercado está diseñado para ayudarle a encontrar un seguro médico que se ajuste a sus necesidades y a su presupuesto. El Mercado reúne en un solo lugar las opciones de seguros médicos privados para que pueda buscarlas y compararlas. También podría ser elegible para un crédito tributario que reduce su prima mensual de inmediato. La inscripción abierta para la cobertura de seguro médico a través del Mercado comienza el 1 de noviembre, para una cobertura que puede empezar desde el 1 de enero.

¿Puedo ahorrar dinero en las primas de mi seguro médico en el Mercado?

Podría reunir los requisitos para ahorrar dinero y reducir su prima mensual, pero solo si su empleador no ofrece cobertura médica o si ofrece una cobertura que no cumple ciertos estándares. El ahorro en la prima para el que sea elegible depende de los ingresos de su hogar.

¿La cobertura médica del empleador afecta la elegibilidad para ahorrar en las primas a través del Mercado?

Sí. Si su empleador le ofrece una cobertura médica que cumple ciertos estándares, usted no será elegible para un crédito tributario a través del Mercado. Sin embargo, podría ser elegible para un crédito tributario que reduzca su prima mensual, o para una reducción de ciertos costos compartidos, si su empleador no le ofrece cobertura o no ofrece una cobertura que cumpla ciertos estándares. Si el costo de un plan de su empleador que le cubriría solo a usted (y no a otros miembros de su familia) es mayor que el 10.22% de los ingresos de su hogar durante el año (este porcentaje puede cambiar cada año), o si la cobertura que ofrece su empleador no cumple el estándar de "valor mínimo" establecido por la Ley del Cuidado de Salud a Bajo Precio (Affordable Care Act), usted podría ser elegible para un crédito tributario. Un plan de salud patrocinado por el empleador cumple el estándar de "valor mínimo" si la parte de los costos totales de los beneficios permitidos que cubre el plan no es menor del 60% de dichos costos.

Nota: Si compra un plan de salud a través del Mercado en lugar de aceptar la cobertura médica que ofrece su empleador, podría perder la contribución del empleador (si la hay) a esa cobertura. Además, su contribución como empleado a la cobertura ofrecida por el empleador suele descontarse antes de impuestos. Las primas del Mercado se pagan después de impuestos.

¿Cómo puedo obtener más información?

Visite HealthCare.gov (o CuidadoDeSalud.gov en español) para obtener más información sobre la cobertura del Mercado y su costo, su elegibilidad para créditos tributarios y la solicitud en línea. También puede pedir más información a Key HR o a su empleador del lugar de trabajo. Si es elegible para la cobertura de seguro médico a través de su empleador del lugar de trabajo, recibirá la información de inscripción y elegibilidad por separado y posiblemente en otra época del año. Si es elegible para la cobertura de seguro médico a través de Key HR, la información de inscripción y elegibilidad se incluye con este documento. Si no se incluye con esta comunicación, comuníquese con su empleador del lugar de trabajo para obtener detalles.

2

Initial Notice of Your HIPAA Special Enrollment Rights

Loss of other coverage

If you are declining enrollment for yourself and/or your dependents (including your spouse) because of other health insurance coverage or group health plan coverage, you may be able to enroll yourself and/or your dependents in this plan if you or your dependents lose eligibility for that other coverage or if the employer stops contributing towards your or your dependents' coverage. To be eligible for this special enrollment opportunity you must request enrollment within 30 days after your other coverage ends or after the employer stops contributing towards the other coverage.

New dependent as a result of marriage, birth, adoption or placement for adoption

If you have a new dependent as a result of marriage, birth, adoption or placement for adoption, you may be able to enroll yourself and/or your dependent(s). To be eligible for this special enrollment opportunity you must request enrollment within 30 days after the marriage, birth, adoption or placement for adoption.

Medicaid coverage

The Key HR group health plan will allow an employee or dependent who is eligible, but not enrolled for coverage, to enroll for coverage if either of the following events occur:

Termination of Medicaid or CHIP coverage. If the employee or dependent is covered under a Medicaid plan or under a state child health plan (CHIP) and coverage of the employee or dependent under such a plan is terminated as a result of loss of eligibility.

Eligibility for premium assistance under Medicaid or CHIP. If the employee or dependent becomes eligible for premium assistance under Medicaid or CHIP, including under any waiver or demonstration project conducted under or in relation to such a plan. This is usually a program where the state assists employed individuals with premium payment assistance for their employer's group health plan rather than direct enrollment in a state Medicaid program.

To be eligible for this special enrollment opportunity you must request coverage under the group health plan within 60 days after the date the employee or dependent becomes eligible for premium assistance under Medicaid or CHIP, or the date you or your dependent's Medicaid or state-sponsored CHIP coverage ends. To request special enrollment or obtain more information, please contact the Key HR Benefits Team at 800.922.4133 or Benefits@KeyHRO.com.

Pérdida de otra cobertura

Si rechaza la inscripción para usted y/o sus dependientes (incluido su cónyuge) porque tienen otro seguro médico o cobertura de un plan de salud grupal, es posible que pueda inscribirse usted y/o inscribir a sus dependientes en este plan si usted o sus dependientes pierden la elegibilidad para esa otra cobertura o si el empleador deja de contribuir a su cobertura o a la de sus dependientes. Para ser elegible para esta oportunidad de inscripción especial, debe solicitar la inscripción dentro de los 30 días posteriores a la fecha en que termine su otra cobertura o en que el empleador deje de contribuir a ella.

Nuevo dependiente por matrimonio, nacimiento, adopción o colocación para adopción

Si tiene un nuevo dependiente como resultado de un matrimonio, nacimiento, adopción o colocación para adopción, es posible que pueda inscribirse usted y/o inscribir a sus dependientes. Para ser elegible para esta oportunidad de inscripción especial, debe solicitar la inscripción dentro de los 30 días posteriores al matrimonio, nacimiento, adopción o colocación para adopción.

Cobertura de Medicaid

El plan de salud grupal de Key HR permitirá que un empleado o dependiente que sea elegible, pero que no esté inscrito, se inscriba en la cobertura si ocurre cualquiera de los siguientes eventos:

Terminación de la cobertura de Medicaid o CHIP. Si el empleado o dependiente está cubierto por un plan de Medicaid o por un plan estatal de salud infantil (CHIP) y esa cobertura termina por pérdida de elegibilidad.

Elegibilidad para asistencia con primas bajo Medicaid o CHIP. Si el empleado o dependiente pasa a ser elegible para recibir asistencia con primas bajo Medicaid o CHIP, incluso bajo cualquier exención o proyecto de demostración realizado conforme a dicho plan o en relación con él. Por lo general, se trata de un programa en el que el estado ayuda a las personas empleadas a pagar las primas del plan de salud grupal de su empleador, en lugar de inscribirlas directamente en un programa estatal de Medicaid.

Para ser elegible para esta oportunidad de inscripción especial, debe solicitar la cobertura del plan de salud grupal dentro de los 60 días posteriores a la fecha en que el empleado o dependiente pase a ser elegible para la asistencia con primas bajo Medicaid o CHIP, o a la fecha en que termine su cobertura de Medicaid o de CHIP estatal, o la de su dependiente. Para solicitar la inscripción especial u obtener más información, comuníquese con el Equipo de Beneficios de Key HR al 800.922.4133 o a Benefits@KeyHRO.com.

3

Premium Assistance Under Medicaid and the Children's Health Insurance Program (CHIP)

If you or your children are eligible for Medicaid or CHIP and you're eligible for health coverage from your employer, your state may have a premium assistance program that can help pay for coverage, using funds from their Medicaid or CHIP programs. If you or your children aren't eligible for Medicaid or CHIP, you won't be eligible for these premium assistance programs but you may be able to buy individual insurance coverage through the Health Insurance Marketplace. For more information, visit www.healthcare.gov.

If you or your dependents are already enrolled in Medicaid or CHIP, contact your State Medicaid or CHIP office to find out if premium assistance is available.

If you or your dependents are not currently enrolled in Medicaid or CHIP, and you think you or any of your dependents might be eligible for either of these programs, contact your State Medicaid or CHIP office or dial 877.KIDS.NOW or visit www.insurekidsnow.gov to find out how to apply. If you qualify, ask your state if it has a program that might help you pay the premiums for an employer-sponsored plan.

If you or your dependents are eligible for premium assistance under Medicaid or CHIP, as well as eligible under your employer plan, your employer must allow you to enroll in your employer plan if you aren't already enrolled. This is called a "special enrollment" opportunity, and you must request coverage within 60 days of being determined eligible for premium assistance. If you have questions about enrolling in your employer plan, contact the Department of Labor at www.askebsa.dol.gov or call 866.444.EBSA (3272).

For more information on special enrollment rights, contact either:

Si usted o sus hijos no son elegibles para Medicaid o CHIP, no serán elegibles para estos programas de asistencia con primas, pero podrían comprar un seguro médico individual a través del Mercado de Seguros Médicos. Si reúne los requisitos, pregunte a su estado si tiene un programa que pueda ayudarle a pagar las primas de un plan patrocinado por el empleador.
